A.explanation: A proton is a hadron made of three quarks ($uud$), so it is not elementary and not a lepton.

B.explanation: A neutron is a hadron made of three quarks ($udd$), so it is not elementary and not a lepton.

C.explanation: An electron is a fundamental particle with no quark structure and belongs to the lepton family with neutrinos.

D.explanation: A quark is an elementary particle, but quarks form a separate family from leptons and combine to make hadrons.

hints: Notice the question asks for both elementary and lepton - recall that hadrons made of quarks fail the first test.
Connect proton and neutron to their $uud$ and $udd$ quark content, which makes them hadrons rather than leptons.
Compare the electron with the quark as two different families of fundamental fermions to decide which family is called leptons.
walkthrough: Identify what is given: proton, neutron, electron and quark, and the test is which one is both elementary and in the lepton group.
State the rule: elementary fermions are divided into quarks and leptons, while particles made of quarks are called hadrons and are not elementary.
Check proton: it has quark structure $uud$, so it is a baryon and hadron, not a lepton.
Check neutron: it has quark structure $udd$, so it is also a baryon and hadron, not a lepton.
Check electron: it has no quark structure, is fundamental, and is a member of the lepton family along with neutrinos.
Check quark: it is fundamental but it belongs to the quark family, not the lepton family.
Therefore the electron satisfies the description. This is option C.
